hook.h2: Wind, earthquake and fire came, and He was in none of them
hook.text: Our Father said, "Go out and stand on the mountain before me; I am about to pass by." A great, powerful wind tore into the mountains and shattered rocks before our Father, but he was not in the wind. After the wind an earthquake, but he was not in the earthquake. After the earthquake, a fire, but our Father was not in the fire. After the fire, the sound of a gentle whisper.
father: "Go out and stand on the mountain before me; I am about to pass by."
hook.note: Elijah had asked to die a few days earlier, and our Father's first answers to him were sleep and food, not correction. When He finally spoke, He let the loud things pass first — the wind, the quake, the fire — and He was in none of them. If the noise is the loudest thing in your day, this is the passage that says His voice is not competing with it. He speaks under it.

short350: You have wanted a Father your whole life. Not a doctrine about Him. Not a distant power. A Father — His voice, His heart turned toward you.
Father's Heart Bible is the first Bible in print where you can see who is speaking. Our Father's words in BLUE. The Son's in RED. The Spirit's in PURPLE.

For a hundred and twenty-five years, red letters have shown the Son speaking. Our Father speaks more than three times as often — 125,457 words across 5,623 verses — and every one of them has been printed in the same black ink as the genealogies. More than one word in four of the Bible is a divine person speaking. The color marks ownership, not quotation: His words stay His on any lips that carry them faithfully, words He never spoke are never colored, and narration stays black.

Elijah asked to die under a broom tree, and our Father neither rebuked him nor argued. He let him rest and fed him. Then came wind, earthquake and fire — and our Father was in none of them. He was the gentle whisper afterward.
That is what this Bible was made to do. Not to tell you about a Father who speaks, but to show you where He already has.

A word about what this book is and is not. Anxiety, depression, PTSD and panic are real conditions, and this Bible is not a treatment for them and does not replace one. It makes no promise about your symptoms. It was not made because someone decided anxious people need a special Bible; it was made because the ordinary black-ink page hides how often our Father speaks, and on a hard day that is the difference between reading about Him and hearing Him.

Nothing here suggests that fear is a failure of faith. Elijah had just watched fire fall from heaven and still wanted to die. Job said what he said. David wrote whole psalms from the floor. Scripture is unembarrassed by all of it, and so is the Father in it.

He is not distant. He is not disappointed. He is your Heavenly Father, and He delights in you as His beloved child. If father is not a word of comfort for you, this Bible is especially for you: the Father revealed here is no projection of broken human fatherhood, but the original, from whom every family in heaven and on earth takes its name.

An introduction opens each book, a Father's note closes each with a short prayer, and 1,354 notes serve the reader, not the scholar. A presentation page carries their name. Six by nine, hardcover, full color throughout.
A fresh translation from the original Hebrew, Aramaic, and Greek — complete, 66 books and 31,085 verses. A gift, a keepsake, an heirloom.
Receive the Father. Hear His voice. His heart is for you.

long.h: Receive the Father. Hear His voice. His heart is for you.
body: The Peace Bible is a color coded Bible for overcoming anxiety, depression, PTSD and panic — the first Bible in print where you can see who is speaking.
Our Father's words in BLUE. The Son's words in RED. The Spirit's words in PURPLE.

It is the complete Father's Heart Bible™ — 66 books, 876 pages, the same translation carried in every edition. What is made for this reader is the cover and the pages that open the book. It is not a treatment, not a program, and not a promise about your symptoms.

long.h: Some days the noise is louder than anything else. Your Father speaks under it, not over it.
body: Days after he had seen fire fall from heaven, Elijah sat under a lone broom tree in the wilderness and asked to die. Our Father did not rebuke him and did not argue with him. He let him sleep. Then He fed him, and said the journey was too much for him. “Get up and eat—the journey is too much for you.” — 1 Kings 19:7.

Wind, earthquake and fire came, and your Father was in none of them. He was the quiet voice that came afterward. It is a devotional Bible for daily Bible reading and intimacy with God, so you hear Him for yourself.

Notice the order in that chapter, because it is the whole reason this edition carries the name it does. Rest came first. Food came second. Speech came last, and quietly. Our Father did not treat a man at the end of himself as a man with a doctrinal problem.

long.h: What this Bible does not claim
body: It does not claim to cure anything. Anxiety, depression, PTSD and panic are real conditions with real treatment, and a Bible is not a substitute for a doctor, a therapist, medication, or the people around you. If you are in crisis, please tell someone today — in the United States, call or text 988.

It does not suggest that fear is a failure of faith. That idea has done a great deal of harm, and Scripture does not support it. Elijah wanted to die. Hannah wept until a priest misjudged her. The psalms are full of people saying the worst of it out loud and being answered rather than corrected.
What it does is simple and checkable: on every page, our Father's own words are set in BLUE, so on a day when you have very little in you, you can find His voice without hunting for it.

long.h: A three color Bible: red letter, blue letter, purple letter
body: For a hundred and twenty-five years, the red letter Bible has shown you the Son speaking. Our Father speaks more than three times as often — 125,457 words across 5,623 verses — and every one of them has been printed in the same black ink as the genealogies. He has been speaking the whole time. No Bible has ever shown you where.
Our Father's words in BLUE. The Son's words in RED. The Spirit's words in PURPLE. More than one word in four of this Bible is a divine person speaking.

The color is a mark of ownership, not of quotation. His words stay His on any lips that carry them faithfully, and words He never spoke are never colored. Narration stays black. You can see it for yourself before you buy anything: every word is free to read at fathersheartbible.com/read.

God is our Father. Not a role He plays. Father is who He is, and Father is His name, the name Jesus came to reveal: “I revealed your name to those you gave me from the world” (John 17:6). This translation lets the Hebrew and Greek speak the distinction they always made: God as Father, Abba Father, your Heavenly Father — and you, His beloved child.

Notice who, in Scripture, speaks of Him only as a distant deity and never as Father: the serpent in Eden, Pharaoh, the accusers in Job, the tempter in the wilderness. The enemy's strategy has not changed since the garden — to make the Father seem distant, demanding, and disappointed.

If the word father is not a word of comfort for you, this Bible is especially for you. The Father revealed here is no projection of broken human fatherhood. He is the original, from whom every family in heaven and on earth takes its name.

faq.q: What makes the Peace Bible different from the other editions?
faq.a: It is the complete Father's Heart Bible™ in Divine Voice Color — the same translation, the same 876 pages, the same 1,354 study notes as every other edition. What is made for this reader is the cover and the pages that open the book: a word written for this reader, and passages on intimacy, identity, and inheritance chosen for where they are. We would rather tell you that plainly than claim notes or prayers that are not in it.

faq.q: Is this the whole Bible, or a selection?
faq.a: The whole Bible. 66 books, 1,189 chapters, 31,085 verses, Genesis to Revelation, nothing abridged — 876 pages of it, in full color throughout.

For a hundred and twenty-five years red letters have shown the Son speaking. Our Father speaks more than three times as often — 125,457 words across 5,623 verses — and until now those words were printed in the same black ink as the genealogies. In Divine Voice Color you see who is speaking: our Father's words in BLUE, the Son's in RED, the Spirit's in PURPLE. More than one word in four of the Bible is a divine person speaking. The color marks ownership, not quotation — His words stay His on any lips that carry them faithfully, and words He never spoke are never colored.

faq.q: Can I read it before I buy a copy?
faq.a: Yes, all of it. Every word of the Father's Heart Bible™ is free to read at fathersheartbible.com/read, in twenty-five languages, with the color on the page exactly as it is in print. English and Telugu can also be listened to. Nobody has to buy anything to receive our Father's voice.

faq.q: Will this Bible cure my anxiety or depression?
faq.a: No, and we will not say otherwise. These are real conditions, and Scripture is not a substitute for a doctor, a therapist, medication, or the people who love you. This is a complete Bible with our Father's own words marked on every page, so that His voice is easy to find on a day when very little is easy. If you are in crisis, please reach out to someone today — in the United States, call or text 988.

faq.q: Does it teach that anxiety is a lack of faith?
faq.a: It does not, anywhere. The opening pages point to Elijah, who asked to die days after seeing fire fall from heaven, and our Father answered him with sleep and food before He answered him with words. Scripture is full of people saying the worst of it out loud without being corrected for it, and this translation does not soften that.

faq.q: Is it a topical Bible with anxiety verses collected in the back?
faq.a: No. It is the complete Bible, Genesis to Revelation, in the same 876 pages as every other edition — no appendix of verses, no reading plan for symptoms. The opening pages carry passages on intimacy, identity and inheritance chosen for this reader; everything after that is the whole Bible in its own order.

faq.q: Would it be a good gift for someone going through a hard season?
faq.a: It can be, with one caution: give it as a Bible, not as a prescription. A person in the middle of it can hear “here is the answer to your problem” in a gift, however it was meant. The presentation page carries their name and yours, which is usually the better thing to say.
